text:
Michael Brandsegg-Nygård came into this season with one NHL point in 14 games. Through 21 games of his second try he has 4 goals and 11 points, plays more than 15 minutes a night, and has thrown 99 hits, which is a lot for anyone and remarkable for a 21-year-old winger from Oslo.

The underlying work is better than the line. His 7.3 expected goals say he gets to the net, and with him on the ice at five on five Detroit controls about 55% of shot attempts and is nearly five points better than without him. Four goals on those chances is light; finishing usually catches up with a shooter whose release is in the top tenth of the league by EDGE speed.

For context, forwards picked 10th to 20th since 2005 have scored a median 0.35 points a game in their first full season. He's at 0.52. The first Norwegian taken in the first round looks like a regular, and the Red Wings, losers of six of seven before Saturday, need his kind of shift.
